comment: The product stack a NEW generated application can be built on: the single source for package names, exact published versions, what each component requires, whether it is supported, and the rules agents are given. Read by src/stack.js (factory, gate, prompts) and src/providers/offline.js (templates). Versions were verified against the npm registry; unsupported components record the verified blocker and the next step.

appport.label: AppPort
appport.summary: Capability discovery and invocation: the app's operations as declared, authorized capabilities (required for every new app).

feltdb.label: FeltDB
feltdb.summary: Durable, transactional application state: the app's authoritative store survives restarts.
rules: Durable state (FeltDB, selected): the app's authoritative state lives in FeltDB (@feltdb/core). Open it once at startup with createFeltDB({ namespace: '<app>', mode: 'local', path }) where path comes from process.env.DATA_DIR (default './data'), use db.collection(name) with insert/get/find/all/update/delete (all async) and db.transaction for multi-record changes, and db.close() on shutdown. Never pass memory: true. At startup record the store's schema version: put { id: 'schema', version: <n> } in the 'app_meta' collection (FeltDB writes nothing to disk before the first write; this makes the store observable and versions it).
FeltDB is the ONLY store: no in-memory copy of records, no cache, no second database. The HTTP API and every AppPort capability call the same store functions over FeltDB.

The app must be the sole writer of its DATA_DIR. FeltDB 0.11.9 does not enforce its documented single-writer lock (a second process's write was observed to succeed), so the app enforces it itself: at startup create <DATA_DIR>/.writer.lock exclusively (fs.openSync(path, 'wx')) holding its pid, refuse to start (exit non-zero) when a live process already holds it, replace it only when that pid is gone, and remove it on shutdown. Strip FeltDB's internal __version field from API results.

Test durability in test/feltdb.test.js: write through the app, close it, then read the records back with a fresh createFeltDB on the same path (read-only use) and through a restarted app; and show that a second instance on the same DATA_DIR refuses to start.

@feltdb/core 0.11.9 sends anonymous usage telemetry to feltdb.com unless FELTDB_TELEMETRY=0 (the factory sets it to 0 for everything it runs). State this in the README and DEPLOY.md with the switch; do not hide it or silently change the package default.

distribution.label: Distribution Protocol
distribution.summary: Signed, verifiable artifact distribution: publish releases whose bytes and publisher anyone can verify.
rules: Signed distribution (Distribution Protocol, selected): use @distribution-protocol/protocol for every release the app publishes. Sign with signRelease(manifest, privateKey, { keyId }) where privateKey = crypto.createPrivateKey(process.env.PUBLISHER_PRIVATE_KEY) (PKCS#8 PEM, Ed25519) and keyId from PUBLISHER_KEY_ID; the manifest has protocol 'distribution/1', product { id: 'product://<publisher>/<name>', name, version }, publisher { id: 'publisher://<publisher>' } from PUBLISHER_ID, artifacts [{ id, mediaType, digest: digestOfBytes(bytes), size, target: { os: 'any', arch: 'any' } }], interfaces [], permissions [], requirements []. Without PUBLISHER_PRIVATE_KEY, publishing is refused; reading and verifying still work.

Verify with verifyRelease(release) AND by requiring release.signature.publicKey to equal exportPublicKey of the app's own publisher key (verifyRelease alone proves only that some key signed); check artifact bytes with verifyArtifactBytes(bytes, artifact). Report { valid, reason } and never treat an unverified release or unmatched bytes as valid.
Never put the private key in source, in a capability description, in a response or in the browser.
Test in test/distribution.test.js: publish, verify, a tampered manifest is rejected, wrong artifact bytes are rejected, and a release signed by another key is rejected.

authboundry.label: AuthBoundry
authboundry.summary: Authentication, authorization and delegation as an authority boundary.
authboundry.blocker: The AuthBoundry authority server could not be verified: `authboundry init` and its FeltDB session bridge work, but `authboundry serve` (1.15.3, linux-x64, with and without --upstream, with AUTHBOUNDRY_FELTDB_PATH set) never opened its listening port and produced no output. @authboundry/core 1.15.3 also pins @feltdb/core 0.11.5 and @appport/services 0.3.2 exactly, which conflict with this stack's FeltDB 0.11.9.
authboundry.next: Verify the exact `authboundry serve` invocation, environment and bridge lifecycle on a supported machine; capture a sign-in → /auth/session → /auth/authorize grant and denial round trip; and resolve the pinned @feltdb/core / @appport/services versions. Then add AuthBoundry as its own tested increment.

services.label: AppPort Services
services.summary: API keys, durable jobs, webhooks and secrets.
services.blocker: @appport/services 0.4.11 executes effects only after an AuthBoundry ServiceAuthorizer allows them (without one, API-key management fails closed), and AuthBoundry is not yet supported. An app-owned substitute authorizer would be a second authorization authority, so none is generated.
services.next: Support AuthBoundry first (see its blocker), then add Services on its intended AuthBoundry authorization path as a separate, tested increment.

appboundry.label: AppBoundry
appboundry.summary: Application packaging, verification and execution integration.
appboundry.blocker: Not a broken package: `appboundry build` packages the contract-driven AppPort model (appboundry.contract.json, appport.implementation.json and a WASM artifact, created interactively by `appport add`), which does not fit the factory's code-defined AppPort boundary.
appboundry.next: A separate integration design: how a generated app adopts the contract-driven model (or how AppBoundry packages a code-defined boundary), with a non-interactive build.
